note: Built-in man-hour factors by PROJECT TYPE and TRADE GROUP (owner comment 62): the productivity of a trade is not the same on a residential, an industrial or an oil & gas project. 1.00 = the library norm; 1.20 = 20 % more man-hours per unit (lower output per day, longer duration); 0.90 = 10 % fewer. Every project type has its own number for every trade. General construction practice for work in Egypt - not measured on a specific project. The planner's own factor, typed on the screen, replaces the built-in one.

groups.label: Earthworks
groups.why: Machine-driven work: fastest on open sites and simple housing plots; slower inside working plants, beside the sea and on airside.

groups.label: Infrastructure — roads, networks & bridges
groups.why: Road and utility-network work is fastest on open infrastructure corridors; slower inside built-up plots, live plants, ports and airside, where space, permits and existing services slow the crews.

groups.label: Concrete structure (formwork, rebar, concrete, precast)
groups.why: Repetitive floors are fastest; heavy foundations, thick sections, embedded items and marine exposure need more man-hours.

groups.label: Structural steel
groups.why: Light, repetitive frames are fastest; heavier members, work at height and permit-controlled sites slow erection.

groups.label: Architectural finishes & masonry
groups.why: Repetitive apartments and plain industrial finishes are fastest; hospitals and terminals carry higher finish standards and more co-ordination.

groups.label: MEP building services (electrical, HVAC, plumbing, fire fighting, ELV)
groups.why: Service density drives the hours: light in housing, heavy in hospitals, terminals and plants.

groups.label: Mechanical, piping, instrumentation, insulation & coating
groups.why: Process work is slowest on oil & gas and power sites: welding quality, inspection hold points and permits.

groups.label: Testing & commissioning
groups.why: More systems, more witnesses and more documents on hospitals, airports, plants and oil & gas.
